Marina Bay has featured at least one safety car in every single edition since its 2008 debut.
Drivers can lose up to three kilograms of body weight during the grueling two-hour race.

headline: Singapore GP: Paddock opens at Marina Bay as Antonelli handles title spotlight
whyCareReason: Formula 1 personnel unpack at Marina Bay under Singapore's tropical heat, with 19-year-old Kimi Antonelli commanding an 88-point championship buffer.
teaser: Wednesday 30 September: Garages light up along the Singapore waterfront. Antonelli, Russell, Hamilton, and Norris face the world press ahead of Friday practice.
story:
Why this one matters: The Formula 1 paddock sprang to life on Wednesday afternoon along the Singapore waterfront as freight containers opened and floodlight towers were tested ahead of the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix.

All eyes were fixed on the Mercedes hospitality suite, where championship leader Kimi Antonelli faced a packed press conference. Fresh off his dominant pole-to-flag victory in Baku, the 19-year-old rookie carries 317 points and an 88-point advantage over teammate George Russell. Antonelli remained composed, noting the physical toll of Marina Bay's 19 turns and extreme humidity.

Down the pit lane, Ferrari and McLaren engineers spent Wednesday verifying high-downforce aero configurations. With track temperatures consistently exceeding 30 degrees Celsius and safety car probabilities near 100 percent, Singapore presents the greatest tactical hurdle on the autumn calendar.
stakes: Antonelli seeks to extend his 88-point championship advantage while Ferrari and McLaren bring downforce upgrades to challenge Mercedes.
rivalryAngle: High-downforce street battle tests Mercedes straight-line superiority against McLaren and Ferrari agility.
